item.title: Trump says "we don't need a deal with Iran"
item.description: President Trump says the war with Iran has been won and "we don't need a deal," as Tehran sticks to its demands and continues attacking ships.

item.title: Van Hollen will challenge Schumer for Senate majority leader
item.description: Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland announced Thursday that he will challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader.

item.title: GOP lawmakers press Huang and Lutnick to testify over Nvidia
item.description: Republicans on Capitol Hill are negotiating for now-resigned Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang​ to appear before Congress.

item.title: Crews begin excavating site of building collapse in Brooklyn
item.description: At least eight people were killed​ after a building collapsed Wednesday in Flatbush, Brooklyn.

item.title: NAACP official on Mississippi electing Scott Colom as its first Black senator since the 1800s
item.description: CBS News projects that Democrat Scott Colom will defeat Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith to become the first Black senator from Mississippi since the 1800s. Charles Taylor, executive director of the Mississippi State Conference of the NAACP, joins CBS News to discuss the significance of Colom's win.

item.title: Legal expert on White House warning to Democrats over possible Trump investigations
item.description: The White House is warning Democrats that threats to investigate the Trump administration could constitute an abuse of power as the new Congress prepares to take office. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson explains.

item.title: How Nvidia's stock decline could impact your retirement savings
item.description: Nvidia's stock declined sharply this week amid Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which led to his resignation as CEO. The decline is set to hit retirement accounts invested in funds that own Nvidia shares. Sabrina Escobar, a reporter at Barron's, joins "The Daily Report" to break it down.

item.title: No charges for driver who plowed truck into field during Kansas youth soccer game, killing 2
item.description: A district attorney in Kansas said he will not be pressing criminal charges against a woman who drove a pickup truck into spectators and bystanders on the sidelines of a youth soccer match last month. Two people were killed, including a 6-year-old. Tom Hanson has more.

item.title: What could happen to AI development and chip production as Huang resigns from Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO of Nvidia raises questions about the future of AI development and chipmaking. CBS News' Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Men 50-69 should get screened for prostate cancer every 2 years, American Cancer Society says
item.description: The American Cancer Society has updated its screening guidance for prostate cancer. Dr. Christopher Anderson, urologist and prostate cancer expert at NewYork-Presbyterian/Columbia University Irving Medical Center, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss the changes.

item.title: Examining Jensen Huang's swift and stunning fall from grace at Nvidia
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after admitting to an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. There are also reports he may have had affairs with two other women. The ramifications of his resignation could have huge national consequences for the future of his company and America's edge in the artificial intelligence race. Jo Ling Kent has more.

item.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine's Starshield use limited again amid meeting with U.S. envoys
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday that the country's Starshield defense system has been limited again as President Trump's senior envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, hold separate talks with both Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin. CBS News' Eleanor Watson reports.

item.title: Extended interview: Ole Miss students describe alleged racial harassment seen in viral video
item.description: A group of University of Mississippi roommates are speaking out after a doorbell camera captured two White students making monkey gestures and sounds outside their apartment. In an extended conversation with Jericka Duncan, the Black students reflect on the alleged racial incident and urge others to "be mindful of their actions."

item.title: Hegseth awards medal to soldier who reprimanded group near tomb
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded a medal to the service member who reprimanded his group for making noise at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier​.

item.title: Trump says Vance should focus solely on domestic corruption
item.description: President Trump posted on social media Thursday that he asked Vice President JD Vance to "focus his complete and total attention" on domestic corruption. Washington Sun senior editor Dave Levinthal and Semafor congressional reporter Nicholas Wu join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: D.C. gunman appeared to vent about problems with luxury condo
item.description: An X account associated with D.C. shooting suspect Matt Lambert was filled with complaints about mold, rodents and disrepair in his unit in the condo building.

item.title: 1 killed, 4 injured in shooting in D.C.; suspect is dead
item.description: The suspect, identified as a 55-year-old doctor, was found dead in his apartment from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said.

item.title: Drunken raccoon merch raises money for local animals that need help
item.description: Last year, a raccoon broke into a Virginia liquor store and sampled lots of spirits before passing out next to the toilet. The internet was delighted, and a local shelter turned that moment into merch, raising money for other animals in the area.

item.title: The role of new right populism in the GOP's future
item.description: Oren Cass, founder and chief economist at the conservative think tank American Compass, joins "The Takeout" to discuss the future of populism in the Republican Party.

item.title: Storm front to bring possible hail, tornadoes to Northeast
item.description: A big storm that was hitting the Northeast on Thursday could bring tornadoes, hail and heavy rain to the region, which could then see a steep drop in temperature, with many areas forecast to dip well below freezing. Rob Marciano has more.

item.title: Pope Leo calls on followers to "value women" and "respect girls"
item.description: Pope Leo visited Peru on Thursday, where he said he learned "what it means to be a shepherd" when he had lived and served in the country for several decades. He gave an emotional speech in which he denounced the culture of "machismo" and called on followers to "value women." Chris Livesay has more.

item.title: Cruise ship detained by Coast Guard in Miami cleared to sail
item.description: The MSC Poesia was detained in Miami earlier this month after the Coast Guard "identified deficiencies with systems on board the vessel."

item.title: Suspected D.C. gunman who killed 1, wounded 4 identified as a doctor, police say
item.description: A gunman killed one person and wounded four others when he opened fire in a gym in Washington, D.C., and then later from his penthouse balcony, police said. The suspected shooter, a 55-year-old doctor, then took his own life, authorities said. Nicole Sganga reports.

item.title: Video shows moment of Brooklyn building's collapse that killed at least 8
item.description: The massive search and rescue effort in the rubble of a collapsed three-story building in Brooklyn ended on Thursday. At least eight people died, including two children. Lilia Luciano has the latest.

item.title: Trump calls for former Apple leader Tim Cook to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Reactions are coming in from the White House and beyond after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of the company on Thursday following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. President Trump suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook as a replacement. CBS News' Jo Ling Kent and Weijia Jiang have more.

item.title: Critics say Lutnick failed to cut off diversion of Nvidia chips to China
item.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under fire from critics asking whether his ties to Chinese companies and friendship with ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang contributed to a lack of oversight over Nvidia AI chip sales.

item.title: 11/12: CBS Evening News
item.description: Suspected D.C. shooter identified as a doctor; Hailstorm could hit East Coast cities.

item.title: USPS adds permanent postage surcharge, citing higher fuel costs
item.description: Still swimming in red ink, the USPS said it will raise some postage prices in 2027 to offset elevated fuel costs.

item.title: What we know about Jensen Huang's resignation so far
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation is effective immediately, less than a week after he admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. CBS News Bay Area's Drew Andre reports, and Paul R. La Monica, Barron's senior markets analysis writer, has more.

item.title: 11/12: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO; Mississippi reacts after Scott Colom wins his Senate race.
